title: Get Zedu featured in 5 press outlets or publications
description: Get Zedu featured in 5 press outlets or publications within 30 days. This means finding news sites, blogs, and magazines that cover Zedu's field, writing short pitches and press releases, and following up with editors. Progress is measured by the number of published articles or mentions about Zedu.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Five press angles built on the completion-rate data, pitched to outlets that cover the beat
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Press outreach only works when the pitch carries something a reporter can use, and Zedu has a genuine finding sitting unused. Cohort programmes with live sessions commonly report completion in the 50 to 85 percent range, against roughly 5 to 15 percent for self-paced equivalents, with the closest thing to peer-reviewed evidence on the self-paced side around 5 percent for MOOCs. The widely repeated 90-plus percent figure comes from vendors selling cohort programmes rather than from research. That gap is the hook, because a trade editor can check it in one click and it is more useful to a reader than another launch post. The work covers five outlets that genuinely cover education, bootcamps or online learning, each with its last three articles read so the pitch matches that outlet's beat, plus one sourced finding matched to each. Deliverable: the outlet shortlist with what each one covers, the pitch per outlet, and a sources appendix where every figure carries its origin and date so an editor can verify it without asking.

upvotes.reason: Press angles built on a number we can actually source are the only ones a journalist can use. Pitching each outlet on the angle it already covers is what turns a favour into a byline.

Cohort programmes with live sessions commonly report completion in the 50 to 85 percent range,...'

downvotes.reason: The '50 to 85 percent vs 5 to 15 percent' completion figures are presented as 'a genuine finding', but in the pitch-notes delivery built on them (reviewed 22 Oct 2026) the source table had zero links; they were cited only as 'Multiple published benchmarks'. Pitching unsourced numbers to reporters under Zedu's name is a risk. Source each figure first.

The core stats don't hold up. The '~5% for MOOCs' figure from the Open Praxis 2024 study comes from its literature review (Jordan 2014), while the study's own four MOOCs show 12-44% completion. The '5-15% self-paced' range has no source.

The completion figures can't survive an editor checking them, so the promised 'verify in one click' doesn't hold yet; same issue already documented on the pipeline goal's version. What works better: five outlets with confirmed beats, one finding each sourced to a named study or to Zedu's own published behaviour.

This proposed angle calls the completion-rate ranges a genuine finding, but the review trail says the cited table had no source links and the roughly 5% figure is not the cited study's measured result. The accepted press approach already requires claims to be source-checked and leaves unsourced metrics out. Pitching these figures risks misleading editors; the angle should be rewritten around a verifiable product use case or wait until primary sources support each number.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Prepare a claims-cleared press pack and five outlet-specific pitches for approval
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Build the press material only from facts that can be checked on Zedu pages or approved by the team, without relying on unsourced completion-rate or performance claims. First, make a short claims register with a link and check date for every product statement, and leave unknown metrics out. Then shortlist five publications by recent relevant coverage and public submission route, and draft a tailored pitch for each using a verified product use case. Hand over the claims register, outlet evidence and five unpublished drafts. Nothing is sent to an editor until the owner approves it.

upvotes.reason: For this goal specifically, "Prepare a claims-cleared press pack and five outlet-specific pitches for approval" reaches people who are not yet searching for Zedu by name, and it ends in something an editor can check rather than a post. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
A press pack where every number has been checked against a source is the difference between coverage and a correction. Clearing the claims once means every pitch that follows can reuse it.
Claims register before pitches - no unsourced numbers, every statement checkable

Outlets ignore generic pitches; a claims-cleared pack (only facts Zedu can publicly support) with one tailored angle per named outlet is the approach most likely to land coverage without overstating the product.

The press goal is earned coverage, and a claims register plus five outlet-specific drafts gives editors useful, checkable material while keeping unverified metrics out. Requiring owner approval before sending also fits the goal without claiming coverage that has not happened.

pendingIdeas.title: Create one newsworthy data point: a short survey of educators on how they run cohorts today, published as a small report
pendingIdeas.description: Editors cover findings, not product launches. Approach: run a short, consented survey (8-10 questions) of bootcamp, school and university educators in Nigeria and nearby markets about the tools they use, WhatsApp overload, data costs and what breaks, aiming for at least 50 responses. Publish the aggregate results as a two-page report with the method and sample stated honestly. Pitches then lead with the findings. Done: the questionnaire, the distribution plan, the report template, and the rule that no figure is published from fewer than 50 responses.

upvotes.reason: "Create one newsworthy data point: a short survey of educators on how they run cohorts today, published as a small report" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
